principle: When adding a hashability wrapper, compare or unwrap peer wrappers consistently so equality and hashing preserve the wrapped value contract.
why: Comparing a wrapped value directly with its wrapper can make equal keys compare unequal and break grouping or cache reuse.

principle: When extending model discovery, preserve documented local and offline defaults unless the change explicitly migrates callers.
why: A network-backed default or new optional dependency can break established offline deployments.

principle: Provider override logic must retain discovered registry defaults when inline configuration omits optional fields.
why: Treating an absent override as absence of the model converts a compatible configuration into an unknown-model failure.

description: Bound runtime-wide resource regions on latency-sensitive paths.
principle: Before entering a runtime-wide resource or GC suppression region in a request handler, prove bounded duration, failure handling, and safe cleanup under production load.
why: Latency-sensitive handlers can stall or hang the process when a global runtime region cannot be maintained or finalized safely.

principle: When recreating framework objects, explicitly carry forward derived state that can no longer be recomputed from the transformed inputs.
why: Resetting derived route metadata can silently degrade generated schemas while runtime behavior still appears correct.

principle: Candidate controls must never be loaded.
Deprecated controls must never be loaded.
